paper.title_en: Nuclear mass calculation based on anisotropic kernel ridge regression and $α$-decay chain recursion
paper.abstract_en: Many short-lived or rarely produced nuclei defy direct mass spectrometry, but their masses are constrained by the $α$-decay energies connecting them through decay chains. We combine anisotropic kernel ridge regression (AKRR), an extended Garvey--Kelson relation (GK16), and $α$-decay chain recursion: AKRR learns the residuals between experimental $α$-decay energies and WS4 predictions, GK16 removes residual local fluctuations, and the corrected energies convert a measured anchor mass into the target mass by exact recursion---replacing absolute-mass extrapolation with interpolation of relative decay energies plus exact algebra. The only data-adjusted quantities are the three kernel hyperparameters, fixed by leave-one-out cross validation. For the 22 nuclei whose masses were measured only after AME2003, the $Q_α$ RMSD falls from 169~keV (WS4) to 108~keV (AKRR) and 65~keV (AKRR+GK16), and the mass-excess RMSD reaches 86~keV, versus 348 and 211~keV for WS4 and AKRR. Mass excesses are further predicted for the 122 nuclei with measured $Q_α$ but no directly measured masses.
